title: Old hands return to Blueprint board, new judges and a Pepco veteran to PSC, in political notes
summary: Some familiar faces return to the board overseeing the Blueprint for Maryland's Future, an industry spokesman moves to the government side, and six new district court judges are appointed, in political notes.
content:
by William J. Ford and Christine Condon, Maryland Matters July 28, 2026

by William J. Ford and Christine Condon, Maryland Matters July 28, 2026

It’s as if they never left.

When the Blueprint for Maryland’s Future Accountability and Implementation Board meets Thursday in a virtual session, board members Isiah “Ike” Leggett and Robin Werner will be back in their seats, after they were reappointed by Gov. Wes Moore (D) to new six-year terms. Leggett’s and Werner’s previous appointments expired July 1.

Leggett, the first Black county executive in Montgomery County, has served as the Blueprint board’s chair since it first convened in November 2021. Werner, a director of teaching and learning for public schools in Talbot County, was appointed in August 2025 to replace Mara Doss, a former associate vice president for teaching, learning and student success at Prince George’s Community College.

Leggett and Werner were among 29 people who applied to serve on the board, which is charged with overseeing implementation of the state’s multiyear, multibillion-dollar education reform plan, the Blueprint. The list of applicants was narrowed down to four finalists by the AIB Nominating Committee last month and sent to the governor, who made the final selection.

When the board meets online Thursday, its agenda includes proposed updates to the Blueprint comprehensive plan, which serves as a guide for state agencies, the 24 school districts and other stakeholders to follow and help implement the statewide plan. Any updates to the plan must be done annually by Aug. 1. Some of the changes include new or revised policies adopted by the General Assembly during the 90-day session.

The board will not meet in August but then reconvene on Sept. 17.

The Maryland Public Service Commission’s new communications director hails from Pepco, the Exelon electric company that serves the District of Columbia and parts of Maryland.

Tony Ruffin, who worked at the utility for 16 years, including as external affairs manager covering Prince George’s County, replaces Tori Leonard, who retired at the end of June after more than a decade at the commission.

“I am honored to join the Commission as well as work with Chair [Kumar] Barve, each Commissioner and Commission staff on the important issues before the MD PSC,” Ruffin said in a statement issued Friday. “It’s also a privilege to succeed Tori, whose long, impressive tenure and commitment to excellence sets a high bar but I am confident that the legacy she has left and the incredible talent within the Commission will allow me to make a smooth transition.”

Ruffin, a Washington D.C. native, previously worked in communications roles at Anne Arundel County and Prince George’s County public schools, according to a news release from the commission. He also served as chairman of the Board of Directors of the Prince George’s Chamber of Commerce from 2024 to 2025.

“We are very pleased to welcome Tony to the Maryland Public Service Commission,” said Barve, the chair of the PSC. “Tony brings years of utility, communications, and government affairs experience that we believe will be valuable in this role, and we look forward to his leadership in helping to shape and strengthen public engagement and outreach.”

Gov. Wes Moore (D) announced the appointments Monday of six people to serve in the district courts of Prince George’s and Washington counties.

Daniel Kyungmin Kim, Julia Simone Gagne Rupert, Jessica Lowell Garth and William Carl Isler II will serve as judges in Prince George’s, while Travis William Poole and Mikhaila Miriam Eugenia Mc Nicolls will serve on the Washington County bench. Moore said that with their “years of experience and guided by a wealth of legal expertise, I know all of them will serve our state well.”

Kim currently works in the Prince George’s State’s Attorney’s Office as the assistant chief of the homicide and strategic investigations units. Prior to that,  he worked for 11 years at the Baltimore City State’s Attorney’s Office and spent the majority of that time as an assistant state’s attorney. Kim received a law degree from the University of Baltimore School of Law.

Rupert is an assistant attorney general in the criminal appeals division of the Maryland Attorney General’s office. She has also served as \an assistant section chief in the District of Columbia Office of the Attorney General, an assistant state’s attorney in Prince George’s and a law clerk for Circuit Judge Nicholas E. Rattle. Rupert graduated from the University of District of Columbia’s David A. Clarke School of Law.

Garth has worked in the Prince George’s State’s Attorney’s Office for more than 12 years, which includes work as an intern, the office’s legislative policy director and an assistant state’s attorney. She is currently chief of the office’s special victims unit. She received a law degree at the George Washington University Law School.

Isler has worked for more than 11 years as program counsel in the Office of Compliance and Enforcement for the Legal Services Corp., an independent, nonprofit organization that helps provide legal aid for providers to help low-income residents. Before that, Isler worked as counsel to the Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission. He received a law degree from the University of Maryland Francis King Carey School of Law.

According to the governor’s office, Poole serves as an assistant attorney general and became the supervising attorney for the Western Maryland region, whose work includes representing the Department of Human Services and the Washington County Department of Social Services. In March, the county’s Board of Commissioners unanimously voted to reappoint Poole as a legal representative to the county’s Animal Control Authority. He earned his law degree from the University of Baltimore School of Law.

Mc Nicolls is a co-managing partner at the Hagerstown law firm, Hutchison & Mc Nicolls, established in 2024. Mc Nicolls, originally from Trinidad & Tobago, worked as a public defender in Washington County and also worked in private practice. She received her law degree from the Howard University School of Law.
